title: Acrylamide Health-Based Guidance Value Under a Threshold Paradigm: Non-Neoplastic Endpoints,  Endogenous Background, and Beverage Exposure
content: Background/Objectives: Acrylamide is a process contaminant in heated foods and beverages, with evidence for animal carcinogenicity and human neurotoxicity. Because acrylamide was assessed as a genotoxic carcinogen, the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) applied a margin-of-exposure approach in 2015 without deriving a health-based guidance value (HBGV). This classification is now contested, with a threshold mode of action proposed. Methods: Benchmark dose modeling used National Toxicology Program Technical Report 575 data for four non-neoplastic endpoints. An exploratory HBGV was derived from EFSA’s BMDL10 of 0.43 mg/kg bw/day for peripheral nerve degeneration in male rats, with an uncertainty factor of 100. Results: BMDL10 values ranged from 1.63 to 1.94 mg/kg bw/day, a robust non-neoplastic point-of-departure range. The exploratory HBGV was 4.3 µg/kg bw/day; subtracting an estimated endogenous background of 0.3 µg/kg bw/day leaves a theoretical exogenous budget of 4.0 µg/kg bw/day. Conclusions: The proposed value ex-ceeds average adult dietary exposure, but the margin narrows for highly exposed children. Coffee is the dominant beverage source for adults, yet heavy consumption uses a small fraction of that budget. For public health policy, coffee remains a mitigation target, while children’s narrow margin is driven by solid foods. Mitigation entails trade-offs with other process contaminants.
